meta_description: Aurore is a C++23 UI library for controllers, TVs and touch screens: the Nintendo Switch's look out of the box, on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux, PS4, PS Vita, the Switch and the browser.
sites_playshelf: Your game library, on the console
hero_eyebrow: A Boréale project · fork of borealis
hero_title: A Switch-like interface for your app, on every screen
hero_title_plain: A Switch-like interface for your app, on every screen
hero_lede: Aurore is a C++ UI library for controllers, TVs and touch screens. It looks like the Nintendo Switch's own menus out of the box, and can be restyled into anything else.
hero_shot_alt: Aurore's demo in Cadran, its look: a rail of icons on the left, cards, chips and buttons, the controller's hints at the bottom.
release_none: No release yet: the submodule follows main.
code_title: A screen is a few lines of XML
code_text: Describe the screen in XML, laid out with flexbox; bind its views in C++. The focus moves with the D-pad on its own, touch and mouse work too, and every colour follows the theme.
demo_band_title: The real demo, in your browser
demo_band_text: Aurore's demo compiled with Emscripten: the same code as on a Switch, drawn with WebGL 2. The keyboard, the mouse, a touch screen or the pad on screen; every theme and language.
f_controllers_text: Focus moves on its own with the D-pad; touch and mouse work too, and the footer shows the buttons that do something.
f_layout_text: Every view is laid out by Yoga, described in XML, code only where it matters. gap, flexWrap, a radius per corner.
f_graphics_text: Hardware-accelerated by nanovg: OpenGL, Direct3D 11, deko3d on the Switch, GXM on the Vita, citro3d on the New 3DS, scaled for a TV.
f_components_text: Tabs, recycling lists and grids, settings cells, dialogs, action sheets, toasts, sliders, Markdown, all restyled by a theme.
f_themes_text: Every colour is a theme key. Theme files and folders bring palettes, pictures, logos, icons and decorations, switched while the app runs, with contrast checked.
f_languages_text: One JSON catalogue per language, switched while the app runs; colour emoji and right-to-left text as options.
f_tools_text: A test harness with simulated time and screenshot comparison, an inspector (F12), hot reload of XML and themes, a profiler, an app template.
f_toolbox_text: Logger, animations, timers, background tasks, storage: what an app needs around its screens.
cadran_title: A look of its own, without a line of code
cadran_text: Cadran, the look of PlayGuard and PlayShelf, is Aurore's look: an icon rail, cards, modals, action sheets, vector icons, a light and a dark theme, language and theme switched while the app runs.
screens_title: The demo, in a few looks
consoles_text: The demo shows itself on each console from the desktop: its screen's size, the console's layout and renderer, the console drawn around it. --simulate 3ds, or a tile on the demo's welcome.
console_alt: The demo on the {console}, the console drawn around its screen
shot_cadran: The demo's welcome, with its dashboard
shot_prism: A theme with its own logo and icons
shot_french: In French, switched while the app runs
adds_text: Aurore follows upstream (xfangfang/borealis) and adds fixes and features picked from other forks, and what its apps need: each one opt-in unless it is a fix.
add_themes: Themes: theme files and folders, palettes from one accent, presets, pictures, logos, icons, decorations and particles, all switched live.
add_styles: Styles: per-state styles (focus, pressed, disabled, hover), transitions, data binding and accessibility labels.
add_views: Views: a recycling grid and row, context menus, icon buttons, Markdown.
add_layout: Layout: Yoga 3, gap, flexWrap with focus across the lines, a radius per corner, gradients, safe areas (notches, system bars, a TV's overscan).
add_text: Text: a font scale for every label, shrink-to-fit, clean line breaks.
add_focus: Focus and hints: no focus lost in hidden or destroyed views; steady footer hints.
add_platforms: Platforms: SDL3 beside SDL2 (desktop, browser, Android, iOS), controllers reconnected under SDL, the browser (Emscripten), deko3d's command memory on the Switch.
add_speed: Speed: no relayout for an unchanged text or size, XML attributes registered on demand, unused textures freed.

stack_title: A current stack, checked on every change
stack_text: Read from the repository each time this site is built: the versions from the build files and the notices, the figures from the tests and the CI.
stack_fig_ci: CI jobs on every pull request, consoles included
stack_fig_tests: test cases in the headless harness
stack_fig_refs: reference screenshots compared pixel by pixel
stack_fig_actions: GitHub Actions pinned to a commit
stack_check_sanitizers: The demo runs under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.
stack_check_fuzz: Markdown and theme files fuzzed with libFuzzer, from the corpus the earlier runs grew.
stack_check_deprecated: A build fails on a deprecated API: no deprecated code, no alias kept for later.
stack_check_format: Every source file formatted by clang-format 18.
stack_check_notices: Each bundled library's version checked against its source and listed with its licence.
stack_check_upstream: Every Monday, the bundled components compared with their upstream's latest release; an issue lists those behind.
vs_description: Everything Aurore adds to borealis or changes from it: new features, the differences side by side, the fixes picked from other forks, and what an app changes to move over.
vs_title: Everything borealis does, and what it lacked
vs_lede: Aurore is xfangfang/borealis (its wiliwili branch) renamed and carried on for PlayGuard and PlayShelf. Everything borealis has stays: its views, its platforms, its drivers. Here is what comes on top, and what changed.
vs_compared: Compared: Aurore's main and the tip of borealis' wiliwili, where Aurore starts. No release of Aurore yet.
vs_line_wiliwili: Its branch for wiliwili, where Aurore starts
vs_glance_languages: translation catalogues, switched while the app runs
vs_glance_cpp: the language standard, with RTTI and exceptions
vs_glance_platforms: platforms: the browser joins the seven
vs_new_text: Cadran is always on; the rest is there when an app wants it.
vs_new_cadran_title: Cadran, a look of its own
vs_new_cadran_text: Always on: an icon rail, cards, sheets and dialogs, about sixty vector icons.
vs_new_themes_text: .theme files and folders: a palette from one accent, presets, nine seasons and feasts, pictures, decorations. Every theme's contrast is checked.
vs_new_styles_text: focus:, pressed:, disabled: and hover: attributes, animated transitions, values bound from XML with bind.
vs_new_a11y_text: A role, a label and a value for every view, a focus announcer in 15 languages, two high-contrast themes, a text scale, reduced motion.
vs_new_text_text: Colour emoji, Hebrew and Arabic from right to left, FreeType as an option, a font per label, shrink-to-fit, cached measures.
vs_new_harness_text: Headless, on a simulated clock: gamepad, keyboard, touch and mouse by call, screenshots compared with references, and fuzzing targets.
vs_new_inspector_text: F12 or L3+R3 opens the tree, the box model and the theme lookups over the app; XML and themes reload on save; a bench catches regressions.
vs_new_density_text: Comfortable, compact or dense lengths in dp, compact: attributes for narrow screens, a preset for a small screen in one call.
vs_sides_title: What both have, and how it differs
vs_sides_text: borealis on the left as its wiliwili branch stands, Aurore on the right.
vs_look_look_was: Its own, close to the Switch's
vs_look_look_now: Cadran, the look of PlayGuard and PlayShelf
vs_look_colours_was: A light and a dark theme, set in code
vs_look_colours_now: Every colour a theme key, switched while the app runs
vs_look_layout_now: Yoga 3.2.1, standard flexbox, gap, flexWrap with focus across the lines
vs_look_corners_now: A radius per corner, horizontal gradients, gradients from code
vs_look_highlight_now: Glides from view to view, can fade after a while
vs_look_images_now: Can be decoded in the background; oversized pictures refused before decoding
vs_text_catalogues_was: 4 languages: English, French, Russian, Simplified Chinese
vs_text_catalogues_now: 15 languages, for the library, Cadran, the hints and accessibility
vs_text_lookups_now: No exceptions, safe from any thread
vs_text_fonts_now: Inter and PromptFont, free fonts; Chinese, Japanese and Korean from the system
vs_text_keyboard_was: Enter, Escape, the arrows and little else
vs_text_keyboard_now: Every controller button on a key, remappable
vs_text_focus_was: A hidden box could take it
vs_text_focus_now: Hidden and destroyed views never hold it
vs_build_platforms_was: Desktop, Switch, PS Vita, PS4, Android, iOS, tvOS
vs_build_platforms_now: The same, and the browser (Emscripten, WebGL 2)
vs_build_licence_now: borealis' code Apache 2.0; Cadran GPLv3, and so an app built with Aurore
vs_fixes_text: From other forks of borealis, from PlayGuard's patches, and from Aurore's own work.
vs_fix_counter: The input block counter no longer wraps around.
vs_fix_destroyed: A destroyed view is forgotten as the focus; a lost focus reaches the parent frames.
vs_fix_hidden: Navigation skips hidden frames and sliders.
vs_fix_controllers: Controllers under SDL: closed on unplug, all read again after a reconnect, presses shorter than a frame kept.
vs_fix_recycler: Each recycling list checks its own width; views queued while the deletion pool drains are kept.
vs_fix_fonts: The font parsers read only inside the font's own data.
vs_fix_logger: The logger writes every line out at once.
vs_fix_disabled: A disabled button can no longer be clicked.
vs_pickers_text: Their commits keep their author and their cherry picked from line; others are rewritten with credit in the commit.
vs_move_text: Most apps build and run unchanged once renamed. The guide lists every line, and what to look at on screen afterwards.
vs_move_names: The names: no compatibility layer, every brls name has an Aurore one; a search and replace does it.
vs_move_licence: The licence: Cadran is linked into every app, so an app built with Aurore is GPLv3.
vs_project_docs_text: 19 guides and an API reference on this site, where borealis has its README and a wiki.
vs_project_ci_text: On top of borealis' builds: formatting, the demo under ASan and UBSan, the tests, the docs; actions pinned to commits.
vs_project_releases_text: Conventional Commits and release-please, a changelog, AURORE_VERSION_AT_LEAST in code.
vs_project_security_text: CONTRIBUTING.md for contributors, SECURITY.md for private vulnerability reports.
vs_project_template_text: In the repository, template/: a minimal app for the desktop and the Switch.
vs_project_notices_text: Third-party notices shipped with every app; tools check them and the bundled libraries' versions.
vs_band_text: The guide takes it step by step: the submodule, the build, the resources, the look, the names.
start_1: Build your project as C++23, with RTTI and exceptions.
start_2: Add Aurore as a submodule, and copy its resources folder to your project's root.
start_3: In your CMakeLists.txt, include commonOption.cmake and toolchain.cmake before project(), add the library after it, and link Aurore::aurore.
start_template: Starting from scratch? template/ is a minimal app that builds for the desktop and the Switch.
start_borealis: Coming from borealis? Change the submodule, then rename brls::, <borealis.hpp> and BRLS_ to Aurore's names: a search and replace.
demo_text: On Linux, macOS or Windows; the other platforms' commands are those of the CI.
